name: Nanoneedling / hair microneedle patches

card.summary: Dissolving microneedle patches are a real drug-delivery technology, but no published trial reviewed here tests them for hair growth.
card.note: Published patch studies cover psoriasis, vaccines, insulin and growth hormone, not hair loss.

quick.overview:
Microneedle patches are small arrays of tiny needles, often made of dissolving material, that release a drug into the upper skin layers. The term is used in hair-loss circles for patches said to deliver actives such as minoxidil or growth-factor products to the scalp.

Published research on dissolving patches concerns other uses, such as psoriasis, vaccines, insulin and hormones. No published human trial among the sources reviewed tested a dissolving microneedle patch for hair growth.
quick.mechanism: Dissolving needles penetrate the outer skin layer, then dissolve and release their payload into the skin. Laboratory and small human studies of such patches have examined delivery depth, stability and skin reactions.
quick.risks: A small human study of placebo dissolving patches found them well tolerated, with only mild redness that resolved. Microneedling in general can cause redness, bleeding and, with non-sterile tools, infection. Safety data for scalp hair products specifically were not found.

lead: Microneedle patches are arrays of microscopic needles, typically tens to a few hundred micrometres long, that pierce the outer skin and deliver a drug into it. Dissolving versions are made of water-soluble materials that dissolve in the skin, so nothing needs to be removed afterwards [5][6]. Hair-loss communities use the terms nanoneedling or microneedle patches for products said to deliver actives to the scalp.

Published research on dissolving patches covers delivery of methotrexate for psoriasis in a preclinical model, human growth hormone, insulin in diabetic rats, influenza vaccine in a human study, and mRNA formulations [1][2][4][7][8][9]. No study among those reviewed tested such a patch on hair growth. Wikipedia notes that the claim that microneedling may promote hair growth rests on weak sourcing [11].

paras: Microneedles are grouped as solid, hollow, coated, dissolving and hydrogel-forming types. Dissolving types have tips that dissolve in the skin and may have incomplete insertion or slow dissolution [11]. A layered pyramidal design with flexible pedestals has been reported to improve delivery [7].
No studies found on dissolving microneedle patches for hair growth.

Related human work exists in other fields. A study of fifteen volunteers using placebo dissolving patches reported good tolerability with no pain or swelling and only mild redness that resolved [3]. A clinical study assessed influenza vaccination with a dissolving patch [5], and stability work found influenza vaccine stable in such patches over long storage [6]. Preclinical research includes methotrexate for psoriasis [1], human growth hormone [2], insulin in diabetic rats [4], caffeine in obese mice [8] and mRNA [9]. Meloxicam patches were formulated for arthritis [10].

In general microneedling can cause redness, swelling, pinpoint bleeding and bruising, and non-sterile devices can lead to infection or pigmentation changes [11]. Placebo dissolving patches were well tolerated in a small human study [3].
Hair-loss users and sellers describe patches as a way to deliver actives to the scalp without an injection. The research reviewed here does not test that use.

timeline.event: A Georgia Tech study showed microneedles can penetrate the stratum corneum [11].
A dissolving patch for human growth hormone delivery is reported [2].
A human tolerability study of placebo dissolving patches is published [3].
